facts_restored_to_separate_paragraphs.existing_fact_text: The natural logarithm is continuous, strictly increasing and onto $\mathbb R$, satisfies $\log1=0$, the product and reciprocal laws, and is inverse to the real exponential ([[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]], [[def-natural-logarithm]]).
Every nondecreasing real sequence bounded above converges to the supremum of its range ([[thm-monotone-convergence]]).

Once step 2.1 supplies the Hilbert basis $(u_I)$, the basis sum for any trace-class $T$ is absolutely convergent and equals $\operatorname{tr}T$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).
## Proof
The complex exponential satisfies $\exp(z+w)=\exp(z)\exp(w)$ for all complex $z,w$ and extends the real exponential ([[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]]).

A nondecreasing real sequence bounded above converges to the supremum of its range ([[thm-monotone-convergence]]).
## Proof

For every $z\in\mathbb C$ the series $\sum_n z^n/n!$ converges absolutely, so its value $\exp z$ is defined and the partial sums of $\sum_n|z|^{2n}/n!$ converge to $\exp(|z|^2)$ ([[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]).
The complex exponential satisfies $\exp(z+w)=\exp(z)\exp(w)$ for all complex $z,w$ and agrees with the real exponential on real inputs ([[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]]).

For a trace-class operator $T$ and a supplied Hilbert basis $(e_n)$, $\operatorname{tr}T=\sum_n\langle Te_n,e_n\rangle$ and $|\operatorname{tr}T|\le\|T\|_1$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).
For nonnegative measurable $g_n\uparrow g$, $\int g_n\,d\mu\uparrow\int g\,d\mu$ ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]).
